explain.say: Imagine doing most of the work, paying most of the taxes, and still having the smallest say. In 1789, that is how most French people felt, and they started a revolution. The timeline shows how it unfolded. Let's begin.

explain.say: First, look at these bars. French society had three estates, or groups. Clergy and nobles were tiny groups, but had big privileges and paid little tax. The Third Estate, everyone else, was about 98 percent of the people. Can you see how unequal that looks?

Back to the timeline. In May 1789 King Louis the Sixteenth called the Estates-General, because France was nearly bankrupt. Each estate had one vote, so the Third Estate was always outvoted. On 20 June its members swore on a tennis court to write a constitution. Brave, right?

explain.say: See the castle? On 14 July 1789, crowds in Paris, angry about bread prices and afraid the king's troops would crush them, stormed the Bastille, a royal fortress and prison. It became the symbol of the revolution. Why would people attack a prison?

faq.a: The First Estate was the clergy, the Second the nobles, and the Third everyone else, from rich merchants to poor peasants. The first two were roughly 2 percent of people but held great privileges.
asks: Who was in the Third Estate?

faq.q: Why did Louis XVI call the Estates-General?
faq.a: France was nearly bankrupt after costly wars, including helping the American Revolution, and bad harvests made bread expensive. The king needed new taxes and called the Estates-General in May 1789, for the first time since 1614.

faq.q: What was the Tennis Court Oath?
faq.a: On 20 June 1789, members of the Third Estate, now calling themselves the National Assembly, met on an indoor tennis court and swore not to separate until France had a constitution.
asks: Why did they meet on a tennis court?

faq.a: Parisians feared the king's troops would attack them, and they wanted the gunpowder stored in the Bastille. It was also a symbol of royal power. It fell on 14 July 1789.
The monarchy was abolished in 1792. Louis was tried for treason and executed in January 1793. Historians still debate why the revolution became so violent.
asks: How did the French monarchy end?

facts: The Bastille was stormed on 14 July 1789.
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was adopted on 26 August 1789.
Before 1789, the Estates-General had last met in 1614.

quiz.say: About what share of French people were in the Third Estate?
quiz.why: Everyone who was not clergy or noble belonged to the Third Estate.

wrong.1: Clergy and nobles together were tiny, so the Third Estate was far more than half.
wrong.2: About 2 percent was the clergy and nobles together.

quiz.say: What did the Tennis Court Oath promise?
quiz.why: They swore not to separate until France had a constitution.

wrong.1: The court was just the meeting place.
wrong.2: They wanted to limit royal power, not crown someone new.
